title: Intelligent Identification of Hazard-Based Red Zones, Carrying Capacity Assessment, and Immediate Relocation Needs for Vulnerable Habitations
department: National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), DM Division
description:
• Background India’s disaster-prone regions face recurring hazards such as landslides,floods, coastal erosion, and cloudbursts. Vulnerable habitations often remain in unsafe zones, leading to repeated loss of lives and property.Current relocation efforts are largely reactive, initiated after disasters strike, rather than proactively planned.
• Description The initiative seeks to develop an intelligent, GIS-enabled decision support platform. This platform will dynamically identify and update multi-hazard Red Zones (areas unsuitable for permanent habitation),assess the carrying capacity of safer alternative sites, and prioritize vulnerable habitations for relocation. The system will integrate hazard intensity, population vulnerability, and disaster history to guide evidence-based decisions.
• Expected Solution A robust, AI-driven GIS platform that Maps and updates hazard-based Red Zones in real time, assesses suitability and carrying capacity of safer relocation sites, prioritizes vulnerable habitations for immediate,short-term, and medium-term relocation and provides actionable insights to State Disaster Management Authorities for proactive planning.
summary: Innovation (4/5): draws on ai, gis applied to a disaster management problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (4/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a working prototype is realistic in a 36-hour window. Impact (4/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Disaster Management. Tech Depth (3/5): centers on gis. Sustainability (4/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 21/30 -> Green verdict.

detail.title: Intelligent Identification of Hazard-Based Red Zones, Carrying Capacity Assessment, and Immediate Relocation Needs for Vulnerable Habitations

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a map-based tool that automatically identifies which villages or settlements sit in genuinely dangerous zones (landslide, flood, erosion-prone), checks whether safer nearby land could actually hold them, and ranks which communities need to be relocated first, so disaster authorities can plan relocations proactively instead of scrambling after a disaster hits.
overview.why_it_matters: India's disaster-prone regions keep losing lives and property because relocation only happens reactively, after a landslide or flood already occurred. A proactive, data-driven system that flags dangerous habitations and viable relocation sites before disaster strikes could save lives that reactive planning simply can't.
pain_points: Vulnerable habitations often remain in unsafe zones because there's no systematic, evidence-based way to identify and prioritize them for relocation before disaster strikes.

Relocation planning needs to consider not just hazard risk but whether alternative sites can actually support the population, that carrying-capacity assessment is often missing from ad hoc relocation decisions.
Hazard zones aren't static, they shift with changing conditions (erosion progression, new landslide data), so a one-time assessment isn't enough, it needs to update dynamically.
overview.background: India's disaster-prone regions face recurring hazards such as landslides, floods, coastal erosion, and cloudbursts. Vulnerable habitations often remain in unsafe zones, leading to repeated loss of lives and property. Current relocation efforts are largely reactive, initiated after disasters strike, rather than proactively planned. An intelligent, GIS-enabled decision support platform is needed to dynamically identify multi-hazard Red Zones, assess carrying capacity of safer sites, and prioritize habitations for relocation.
overview.whats_being_asked: An AI-driven GIS platform that maps and updates hazard-based Red Zones in real time, assesses the suitability and carrying capacity of safer relocation sites, prioritizes vulnerable habitations for immediate/short-term/medium-term relocation, and provides actionable insights to State Disaster Management Authorities for proactive planning, integrating hazard intensity, population vulnerability, and disaster history.
expected_solution: Real-time mapping and updating of multi-hazard Red Zones (landslide, flood, coastal erosion, cloudburst risk).
Suitability and carrying-capacity assessment of safer alternative relocation sites.
Prioritization of vulnerable habitations by urgency (immediate, short-term, medium-term relocation).
Actionable, evidence-based insights delivered to State Disaster Management Authorities for proactive planning.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Breakthrough band, driven by combining multi-hazard GIS mapping with population-vulnerability and carrying-capacity modeling into a single decision-support tool, individually each component (hazard mapping, GIS analysis) is established, the integrated relocation-prioritization framework is the genuinely useful, less commonly built piece.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Medium, correctly scored, this is substantially a data-integration and GIS-analysis exercise (combining hazard layers, population data, and site-suitability criteria) rather than deep novel ML, which makes a working prototype genuinely realistic in 36 hours with the right public datasets.

competitive_landscape.note: GIS-based disaster-risk mapping is a recognizable SIH theme, but the specific combination of Red Zone identification, carrying-capacity assessment, AND relocation prioritization into one integrated decision-support tool is less commonly attempted fully, most teams default to just a hazard-risk heatmap.

innovation.note: The integrated combination of hazard mapping, carrying-capacity assessment, and relocation prioritization is a genuinely more complete decision-support framework than a typical single-purpose hazard-risk map.

invention.note: Primarily a GIS data-integration and scoring-model exercise using established public geospatial datasets, not deep novel algorithm development.

technical_feasibility.note: Public hazard datasets (landslide susceptibility, flood zones from government/ISRO sources) and standard GIS tools make a working prototype realistic within 36 hours.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly informs a specific, high-stakes government decision-making process (State Disaster Management Authority relocation planning), a real and well-defined institutional user.

architecture.note: GIS hazard layers, population data, and a scoring/prioritization model combine into a reasonably clean, well-scoped analytical pipeline.

overall_verdict.reasoning: A strong, achievable pick for a team comfortable with GIS tools and public geospatial data, the biggest differentiator opportunity is building the full pipeline (hazard identification through to relocation prioritization) rather than stopping at a hazard-risk heatmap, which is the more common, less complete version of this idea.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Strong public data availability (landslide susceptibility maps, flood-risk zones, census/population data) means the team can build against real Indian geospatial data rather than needing to synthesize everything.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Stopping at a hazard-risk visualization (the easy, common part) without building the carrying-capacity assessment and relocation-prioritization layers (the differentiating, harder part) would undersell the PS's actual ask.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Confirm hour 0: identify a specific real region with available public hazard data (landslide-prone hill states have good public susceptibility mapping) to ground your demo in a real, credible geography rather than a generic or invented area.

idea_0_4: Pick a specific real, disaster-prone region with available public hazard data (e.g. a landslide-prone district in a hill state) to ground the demo credibly.
Source public hazard datasets (landslide susceptibility, flood-zone maps) and population/settlement data for that region.
Assign owners: one on hazard-zone GIS mapping, one on carrying-capacity/site-suitability modeling, one on the prioritization scoring and dashboard.
prototype_4_22: Build the Red Zone mapping layer: overlay hazard susceptibility data onto a map of known settlements in your chosen region.
Build a carrying-capacity assessment for candidate relocation sites (basic criteria: land availability, distance from hazard zone, existing infrastructure proximity).
Build a relocation-priority scoring model combining hazard severity, population size/vulnerability, and disaster history for each identified at-risk habitation.
integration_22_30: Wire the full pipeline: hazard data -> Red Zone identification -> at-risk habitation list -> candidate relocation sites -> priority ranking.
Build a clean GIS-based dashboard visualization showing Red Zones, at-risk settlements, and recommended relocation sites together.
Test the prioritization logic against a few known real disaster-history cases from your chosen region to sanity-check the ranking makes sense.
polish_30_36: Prepare a live demo walking through the full decision-support flow: showing a Red Zone, the settlements within it, and the system's relocation recommendation with reasoning.
Prepare a clear before/after framing: reactive relocation (after disaster) versus this proactive, evidence-based approach.
Be ready to explain your carrying-capacity criteria and how they were chosen, this is a key differentiator judges will want to understand.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Ground the entire demo in a real, named region with real public hazard data, and reference a specific real historical disaster event in that region if one exists, showing how your system would have flagged that risk area proactively before the disaster occurred. That grounding in real geography and history is far more credible than a generic or invented example.

strengths: Strong public data availability (government hazard maps, census data) supports a genuinely evidence-based, credible demo.
The full pipeline (hazard mapping through relocation prioritization) is a more complete and differentiated tool than the common single-purpose hazard heatmap.
weaknesses: Carrying-capacity assessment involves genuinely complex real-world factors (land rights, infrastructure, social/cultural considerations) that a 36-hour model can only approximate.
Relocation is a sensitive, high-stakes real-world decision, the tool needs to be framed carefully as decision support, not an automated relocation order.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: 2 GIS/data-focused to 1 frontend, the geospatial analysis and scoring logic is where the real work and credibility lies.
team_fit.approach: Source and validate your real public hazard dataset in the first hour or two, since the entire demo's credibility rests on being grounded in genuine geospatial data for a real region, not a synthetic or invented map.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: GIS data loading/processing boilerplate, map visualization scaffolding (using libraries like Leaflet or Mapbox), and basic scoring-model code can be built quickly with AI coding assistance.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Deciding what criteria genuinely constitute 'carrying capacity' for a relocation site (land availability, water access, infrastructure, social factors) needs real research grounding, not an arbitrary, AI-invented scoring formula.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-generated carrying-capacity or prioritization model with criteria that aren't grounded in real disaster-management practice risks looking naive to judges from NDRF or disaster-management backgrounds who understand how genuinely complex relocation planning is in practice.

data_resource_availability.status: Public landslide susceptibility maps (from GSI, ISRO Bhuvan), flood-risk zone data, and census/settlement population data are available for many Indian regions, particularly hill states with documented landslide history.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: If detailed real hazard data for a specific region proves hard to source quickly, use published disaster-history reports and general hazard-susceptibility principles to construct a realistic, clearly-labeled representative scenario rather than fully invented data.

judge_qna.question: What real data is this actually built on, versus assumptions?
judge_qna.strong_answer: We used [specific public dataset, e.g. GSI landslide susceptibility data] for hazard mapping and [specific population data source] for settlement data, for [specific region], here's exactly which parts of our model are grounded in real data versus modeled assumptions.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the resolution/granularity of your source hazard data, and how does that limit the precision of your recommendations?

judge_qna.question: How does your system account for the fact that relocation isn't just a land-availability decision, it involves social, cultural, and livelihood factors?
judge_qna.strong_answer: We're upfront that our carrying-capacity model captures physical/infrastructure suitability, not the full social complexity of relocation, which is why we frame this explicitly as decision support for human planners, not an automated relocation directive.
judge_qna.follow_up: What additional data or expert input would you want to incorporate to make the tool more socially informed?

judge_qna.question: How often would Red Zone data need to be updated, and how would that work in practice?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Hazard conditions like erosion and landslide risk shift over time, our architecture is designed to re-ingest updated hazard survey data periodically, though our hackathon build uses a single data snapshot rather than a live-updating feed.
judge_qna.follow_up: What would a real-world data-update pipeline and cadence look like for this system?
